perturbed_solution:
Expanding the first given equation using the distributive property, we have \begin{align*}
&18=(x+y+z)(xy+xz+yz)\\
&=x\cdot(xy+xz+yz)+y\cdot(xy+xz+yz)+z\cdot(xy+xz+yz)\\
&=x^2y+x^2z+xyz+xy^2+xyz+y^2z+xyz+xz^2+yz^2\\
&=xyz+x^2y+x^2z+xy^2+y^2z+xz^2+yz^2
\end{align*}Expanding the second given equation using the distributive property, we have \begin{align*}
6&=x^2(y+z)+y^2(x+z)+z^2(x+y)\\
&=x^2y+x^2z+xy^2+y^2z+xz^2+yz^2-2xyz.\end{align*}We substitute the equation $$6=x^2y+x^2z+xy^2+y^2z+xz^2+yz^2-2xyz$$into the expanded form of the first given equation to get \[18=xyz+6+2xyz=3xyz+6\]or $x+y+z=\boxed{4}$.

errors.rationale: The expansion contains three xyz terms, so the coefficient should be 3. Replacing 3xyz by xyz drops two of those duplicated terms.
The expansion of x^2(y+z)+y^2(x+z)+z^2(x+y) has no xyz term. Introducing -2xyz is an invented negative term.
The problem asks for xyz, not x+y+z. The computed value is xyz=4, so the final variable should be xyz.
